name: alfred-tools
check_batch: run the tests that cover the change and `npm run lint`
not_for: Not for a release, which follows the Release section of `plugin-handling.md`, on the user's word.
settled: A design already settled by a run order or the user's rulings skips the spec and goes to the plan.
checks: - per batch: `npm run lint` and the tests that cover the change;
- `npm run matrix` (real-CLI cases in a throwaway home and account) after a change to install, configure, update
or fix, reading the written `.mcp.json`, account file and settings, never the exit code alone;
- the full `npm test` once, in the background, its output to a log, its tail read, then `npm run validate`.
voice: single dashes, single quotes in prose
commit: its message with no trace of the agent (`.claude/rules/commits.md`)
not_here: - A change in a sibling repo (plugins-marketplaces hosts the `envoydev` marketplace), which follows that repo's own flow.
- Alfred Code's `task-solve` and its seats, stamps and stops, which serve the projects that install the stack.
structure_map: - Source root `scripts/`. An entry is `scripts/<name>.ts`, five lines: `blockingStdio()` and one call of `scripts/<name>/command.ts`.

- A feature folder is `scripts/<name>/`: `types.ts`, `constants.ts`, `command.ts` (reads the arguments and returns the exit code - it reaches the outside world only through `effects.ts`), logic files, `effects.ts`.

- The outside world: `node:fs`, `node:child_process`, the network, `process.env`, `process.versions`, stdin and stdout, the clock - and the `claude` CLI, started only through `scripts/core/claude-cli.ts`.
- Shared code: `scripts/core/`. `scripts/copied/` is outside the shape: CommonJS that a root runs outside the plugin, byte for byte.
- Tests: `tests/<name>.test.ts` at the top of `tests/` (the test command reads only that level), with the fakes beside them.
- The folders written before 2026-11-15 keep effects in several files and constants beside their code; they follow the shape as they are changed.

notes: commands/*.md are the plugin's four slash commands (install, configure, update, fix), each with frontmatter description, argument-hint, disable-model-invocation: true and allowed-tools; the manifest has no commands key, so the default commands/ folder is what loads. SCRIPTS_ROOT is scripts/.

A command runs its work through scripts invoked only via the plugin root (node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/<x>.ts"), each pre-approved in allowed-tools; npm run lint fails a script path that does not go through the plugin root.

Commands that write registrations (install, configure, update, fix) have side effects the user owns; after an edit that touches what they write, run npm run matrix (real-CLI cases in a throwaway home) and read the written .mcp.json, account file and settings, never the exit code alone.
The MCP-server catalog under catalog/ decides what the commands can install; a command cite of a server is checked against it.

Every catalog row is an MCP server (kind: mcp, 14 rows); there are no plugin rows since 0.5.0 (claude-hud, typescript-lsp and csharp-lsp left), and a plugin row returns only when it works in both Claude Code and Cursor.

Each row's routes are a hosted remote (url, authMode, header helper) or a local launch (runtime npx/uvx, package registry, name and pinned version, cutoff); npm run refresh-pins moves the pins under the 7-day release-age gate (rules.ageGateDays, rules.cutoff), and the vendor facts behind each row are in docs/sources.md.

The claude CLI is the only writer of .mcp.json and the account .claude.json (claude mcp add-json/remove/get, claude plugin install/update/uninstall/list --json); the one exception is scripts/mcps-list/mcp-order.ts, a reorder-only rewrite of .mcp.json.
Cursor is a second host: scripts/cursor/cursor-mcp.ts writes <project>/.cursor/mcp.json and ~/.cursor/mcp.json, so both are part of the install and are read beside Claude Code's.
The catalog holds no secret: a hosted key is named by its helper block, which mcp-headers.js reads from .mcps-secrets, and a stdio key is only ever a ${VAR} reference.
Each row's dangerous field lists the risk the row declares; read it in the security read.

The copied files in scripts/copied/ (mcp-headers.js, mcp-bridge.js, serena-context.yml) run outside the plugin on users' machines and are updated by /alfred-tools:update, so they are part of the installed surface.

Retirement: /alfred-tools:update offers once to uninstall the retired plugins (the retired-plugin offers in scripts/update/), and catalog/reserved-names.json (built by scripts/refresh-reserved.ts) lists names alfred-code once registered.
Known problems and their fixes are catalog/fixes.json, with detect and fix functions in scripts/fix/.

The root is the four manual commands under commands/ (install, configure, update, fix); the repo ships no skills, agents, rules or hooks, and the plugin is standalone - it may read what alfred-code left but must never need it.

After a change to install, configure, update or fix, npm run matrix runs real-CLI cases in a throwaway home and account; read the written .mcp.json, account file and settings, never the exit code alone.
There is no usage analyzer: measure use by counting mcp__<name>__* tool calls in the corpus.

The plugin ships four commands - `commands/install.md`, `configure.md`, `update.md`, `fix.md` - each `disable-model-invocation: true`, so it puts no description in every session; each command's work is a script under `scripts/` called as `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/<file>"`, and `allowed-tools` lists read-only calls only.
No skills, agents, hooks, rules or MCP servers ship; a default component folder (`skills/`, `agents/`, `hooks/`, `bin/`, `.mcp.json`) at the root is a packaging finding.

The repo-root `.mcp.json` is a git-ignored, machine-local dev file the kit sync writes; it never ships but a `claude --plugin-dir .` fixture would read it as a plugin MCP server, so the map attributes it to the dev checkout.

PROFILES is one `default` install; no fixture or session-surface tool exists, so install by hand with `claude --plugin-dir .` in a scratch project under an isolated `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and `HOME` in the session scratchpad, never the real account (matrix installs once left records in `~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json` and nested sessions ended logged out).
The plugin states no project facts by design: S5 fixes what each of the four commands is for.

The plugin's dangerous actions are config writes: it writes `.mcp.json`, the account file, Cursor's config and settings, and handles keys and mcp-remote sign-ins - never a key in `.mcp.json`, the plugin never reads, prints or copies `<root>/mcp-remote-v1/`, and the user's settings deny reads of `mcp-remote-v1/` and `.mcps-secrets`; the guard-route map covers these.

The install proof is `npm run matrix` (real-CLI cases in a throwaway home and account, minutes) after any change to install, configure, update or fix, reading the written `.mcp.json`, account file and settings, never the exit code alone.

The catalog is `catalog/tools.json` (one row per tool), `catalog/fixes.json` (one row per known problem, code under `scripts/fix/`) and `catalog/reserved-names.json`; every outside fact a row rests on is in `docs/sources.md` with its URL and date.
`scripts/copied/` files run outside the plugin in a user's root byte for byte and stay CommonJS.
The version lives in `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and is mirrored in `package.json`; `npm run lint` fails on drift.

`npm run validate` runs `claude plugin validate --profile directory --strict` on a scratch copy of the files git would ship; the publish order is validate, a `claude --plugin-dir .` session in a scratch project, then `claude plugin details`.

MARKETPLACE is the `envoydev` catalog in envoydev/plugins-marketplaces (`.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`), which lists the plugin as a github source on envoydev/alfred-tools `main` with no `sha`; `main` is release-only and a merge there with a new version is the release.
Never rename or drop the id `alfred-tools`: every install goes silent.
Plugin CLI behaviour evidence is recorded in `docs/plugin-cli-evidence.md`.
The repo is public: no private project names or absolute local paths in a tracked file (`npm run lint` checks the paths).

No collector, analyzer or per-project report skill exists: collect by route 3 by hand (the raw transcript and its `<session-id>/` folder copied from `~/.claude*/projects/`), count with `jq` / `grep`, and offer `skeleton` only.

The plugin's commands are manual, so its use shows in a transcript as a user-typed `/alfred-tools:<command>` expansion and the `node .../scripts/<file>` Bash calls it makes; there are no skills, agents or hooks to score.

`docs/sessions-investigation/` already holds hand-written evidence folders (for example `preferred-tools-issues-2026-11-10/`), not collector bundles: read them as already-known claims to verify, never as bundles.
ES modules in TypeScript, run by Node's type stripping (engines ^22.18.0 || >=23.6.0): erasable syntax only, and an import names its file with its .ts extension.

scripts/copied/ is CommonJS that a root runs outside the plugin, byte for byte, and tests/matrix/fixtures holds copies a test reads as data: both are left as they are, never scored and never converted.
npm test reads only the top level of tests/ (node --test tests/*.test.ts); tests/matrix and tests/proof run by their own scripts (npm run matrix, npm run proof).
npm run lint is tests/lint.ts, the repo's own lint script; there is no lint or format config file.
typescript and @types/node are exact-pinned dev dependencies; npm run typecheck is tsc -p . over scripts and tests.
The repo is public: no private project names or absolute local paths in a tracked file.
